canonical_question: What should I understand about deciding whether the project or performance owns tempo, and why does it matter in Logic Pro?
clarification_questions: Which should remain unchanged: the project grid, the recorded performance, or the imported file at its native speed?
Is this audio or MIDI, single-track or multitrack, and what are the current Project Tempo mode and region Smart Tempo/Flex & Follow settings?
Is the problem the BPM number, downbeat, bar count, meter, gradual drift, local beat marker, audio speed, stretching artifact, or movement of other project material?

competing_hypotheses.description: Deciding whether the project or performance owns tempo is the correct feature, but the tempo direction, map range, or conformance depth is wrong.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 1

competing_hypotheses.description: The detected BPM, downbeat, meter, beat markers, source metadata, multitrack reference, or half/double interpretation is wrong.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 2

competing_hypotheses.description: A fixed BPM, manual tempo points, tap/region-length calculation, Flex-only edit, alternate source, or no conformance would preserve the music better.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 3

direct_answer: Before changing BPM or enabling conformance, decide which thing should remain musically unchanged: the project grid, the recorded performance, or an imported reference. A BPM number, grid, or beat marker is a hypothesis about musical structure until it is verified by listening.
evidence_needed: The current Logic version, Project Tempo mode, selected region Smart Tempo/Flex & Follow state, source type, file metadata, and analysis source/downmix.
The untouched native-speed source plus the applied map or conformed version, with the beginning, middle, end, and transitions checked against a metronome.
Detected BPM, downbeat, meter, beat-marker placement, Tempo track events, and whether half/double tempo or gradual drift is present.
The user’s report of groove, bar alignment, audio speed/pitch, stretching artifacts, moved regions, and behavior of MIDI, loops, Drummer, automation, and tempo-synced effects.
key_distinction: Before changing BPM or enabling conformance, decide which thing should remain musically unchanged: the project grid, the recorded performance, or an imported reference.
limitations: A displayed BPM or grid alignment does not prove the musical interpretation is correct.
Tempo and beat detection are fallible for rubato, syncopation, weak pulse, pickups, mixed meter, dense polyphony, silence, and ambiguous half/double tempo.
Professional/community sources are context-bound and may disagree.
Exact Logic procedures remain unverified on the owner’s installed build.
This synthesized candidate is not yet promoted to reviewed knowledge.

logic_guidance.starting_point: Begin with no destructive change: identify the intended tempo authority and preserve a baseline.
steps: Save a Project Alternative or duplicate tempo set/region, and document the current Project Tempo mode, region Smart Tempo/Flex & Follow state, analysis source, downbeat, meter, and tempo-dependent tracks/effects.

Duplicate the project or create a Project Alternative, audition the performance against a click, and explicitly choose whether the grid should follow the performance or the performance should follow the grid.
Preview the beginning, middle, end, and every tempo/meter transition against the Smart Tempo Editor or project metronome, then compare against the untouched baseline.
Listen and inspect for: the chosen authority remaining unchanged while later elements follow it naturally.
Stop or back off if: Choosing the wrong authority can stretch good audio or rewrite a useful project tempo map.
Restore the saved Project Alternative and prior Project Tempo/region settings.
